claims.statement: The mitigation action (evict_entitlement_entries) successfully resolved the incident; authorization failures dropped from 31% to 1% within 3 minutes after cache eviction.
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified observability data showing measurable impact
claims.limitation: 1% baseline reflects normal application error rate, not persistent incident

claims.statement: The root cause of the support agent access failures was confirmed to be a stale authorization cache in the customer-records app that served version 41 entitlements for users whose roles had been updated to version 42.
claims.corroboration: Multiple tier-1 sources form complete chain: directory change at 02:10 (m7_e03), failures at 08:30 (m7_e02), version mismatch confirmed (m7_r_traces), mitigation resolved via cache eviction (m7_r_evict). No competing hypotheses remain viable.
claims.limitation: Root cause identification complete; underlying mechanism of why app cache failed to refresh remains undiagnosed but not necessary for incident resolution

next_action.rationale: Mission objective complete. Root cause established: stale authorization cache in customer-records app serving v41 when directory held v42 for 214 role-updated users. Timeline: directory synced 02:10 → incident began 08:30 → eviction mitigation applied and succeeded (31%→1% in 3min). Highest-information authorized next step was taken (evict_entitlement_entries) and was approved and executed by human gate. Incident resolved.
